scorecard.rationale: Two placebo-controlled oral Salvia officinalis extract trials in menopause (Zeidabadi 2020 dry extract, n=59, PSQI 9.4 to 5.6; Dimpfel 2021 fresh-tip extract, n=78) and a dormitory student tea trial versus brown sugar (Rigi 2024, n=128, room-allocated with unequal sugar and baseline typo) report better global sleep scores. An active-controlled primary-insomnia pilot comparing dried sage tea against chamomile was inconclusive (n=30, ISI p=.78/.83, baseline below eligibility) and the Newcastle Parkinson dried-sage pilot reported cognition and salivation without a sleep estimate. No controlled evidence shows insomnia worsening; the non-Parkinson sleep trials sustain a minimal_signal against worsening. The isolated ursolic acid review lists sage among plant sources. It supplies no dried-sage intake or sleep endpoint. The pediatric sleep guideline's Sage mention is a publisher. The Guadalajara follow-up records traditional use of dried common sage. Its insomnia entry concerns cinnamon. The study supplies no individual sleep outcome linked to sage and leaves the existing minimal easing lean anchored to controlled non-Parkinson studies.
